title: ABS Challenges: Triple-A 2025 to MLB 2026
subtitle: Every ABS challenger with MLBAM ids and run values, Triple-A 2025 to MLB 2026
description:
# ABS Challenges: Triple-A 2025 to MLB 2026

MLB adopted the **ABS (Automated Ball-Strike) challenge system** in 2026: the plate umpire still calls every pitch, and the batter, pitcher or catcher can challenge the call, which Hawk-Eye then decides. Baseball Savant has challenge boards for Triple-A from 2025 and for MLB's 2025 spring-training test, so challenge behaviour was recorded for many players **before** the system reached MLB games.

This dataset puts both levels in one table, keyed by the **MLBAM player id**, so the questions can be asked across the jump: do players who challenge well in Triple-A also challenge well in MLB? Who challenges too often, and what does it cost in runs?

Data as of **{built}** (UTC).

## Files

| File | Rows | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `abs_challenges_players.csv` | {rows:players} | All 15 ABS challenge boards listed below, one row per player per board |
| `abs_aaa2025_to_mlb2026.csv` | {rows:bridge_batters} batters + {rows:bridge_catchers} catchers | Players on both the Triple-A 2025 and MLB 2026 regular-season boards (with `n_total_sample` > 0 on each), measures side by side ({rows:bridge_columns} columns) |

### Boards in `abs_challenges_players.csv`

Players listed (total challenges made) per board. Every board is fetched with a minimum of 0 challenges, so players who never challenged are listed too.

| Board | Batters | Pitchers | Catchers |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLB 2025 spring training (the test) | {rows:mlb2025S_batter} ({rows:mlb2025S_batter_chal}) | {rows:mlb2025S_pitcher} ({rows:mlb2025S_pitcher_chal}) | {rows:mlb2025S_catcher} ({rows:mlb2025S_catcher_chal}) |
| Triple-A 2025 regular season | {rows:aaa2025R_batter} ({rows:aaa2025R_batter_chal}) | {rows:aaa2025R_pitcher} ({rows:aaa2025R_pitcher_chal}) | {rows:aaa2025R_catcher} ({rows:aaa2025R_catcher_chal}) |
| Triple-A 2026 regular season | {rows:aaa2026R_batter} ({rows:aaa2026R_batter_chal}) | {rows:aaa2026R_pitcher} ({rows:aaa2026R_pitcher_chal}) | {rows:aaa2026R_catcher} ({rows:aaa2026R_catcher_chal}) |
| MLB 2026 spring training | {rows:mlb2026S_batter} ({rows:mlb2026S_batter_chal}) | {rows:mlb2026S_pitcher} ({rows:mlb2026S_pitcher_chal}) | {rows:mlb2026S_catcher} ({rows:mlb2026S_catcher_chal}) |
| MLB 2026 regular season | {rows:mlb2026R_batter} ({rows:mlb2026R_batter_chal}) | {rows:mlb2026R_pitcher} ({rows:mlb2026R_pitcher_chal}) | {rows:mlb2026R_catcher} ({rows:mlb2026R_catcher_chal}) |

Savant has no boards (checked when building) for the MLB 2025 regular season or Triple-A spring training; the build fails if any of these boards ever appears, so this table stays complete. Triple-A pitchers made almost no challenges in 2025, so the bridge table covers batters and catchers.

## Why this and not Savant's CSV export

Savant's ABS leaderboard offers a CSV download, but that export has 36 columns and **no player id**, only a display name that repeats within a season, so it cannot be joined to Statcast or across levels. The page itself embeds the same rows as JSON with 86-87 fields, including the MLBAM `player_id` and the run-value columns. This dataset is built from that JSON with [savant-extras](https://pypi.org/project/savant-extras/) 0.6.0 (`abs_challenges()`).

## Key columns

`abs_challenges_players.csv` has {rows:columns} columns: the ABS board columns below (names are Savant's own; `game_type` is added by this dataset), then the player columns in the next section. Meanings below other than the three identities follow Savant's column names; see the [Savant ABS leaderboard](https://baseballsavant.mlb.com/leaderboard/abs-challenges) for its definitions.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `challenge_type` | Who challenged: `batter`, `pitcher` or `catcher` |
| `player_id` | MLBAM id (joins to Statcast `batter` / `pitcher` / `fielder_2`) |
| `level`, `year`, `game_type` | `MLB`/`AAA`, season, `R` regular season / `S` spring training |
| `team_abbr`, `parent_org` | Team, and its MLB parent organisation |
| `n_total_sample` | Savant's sample size for the player, the denominator of `rate_challenges` (= `n_challenges` / `n_total_sample`) |
| `n_challenges`, `n_overturns`, `n_fails` | Challenges, won, lost (`n_fails` = `n_challenges` - `n_overturns`) |
| `rate_overturns` | `n_overturns` / `n_challenges` |
| `exp_chal`, `exp_rate_overturns`, `overturns_vs_exp` | Savant's expected values for an average challenger facing the same pitches, and the difference |
| `n_chal_runs`, `exp_chal_runs`, `runs_vs_exp` | Run value of the challenges, expected, and the difference |
| `n_chal_reasonable_opps`, `rate_reasonable_opp_taken` | Savant's count of reasonable challenge opportunities, and the share the player took |
| `n_strikeouts`, `n_walks` | Savant's strikeout and walk counts on the board |
| `*_against` | The same measures for challenges made **against** the player's side |

The build checks that these identities hold on every board: `n_fails` = `n_challenges` - `n_overturns`, `rate_challenges` = `n_challenges` / `n_total_sample`, `rate_overturns` = `n_overturns` / `n_challenges`.

## Player columns added to every row

Every row also carries per-player columns, fetched for **the same level, season and game type as its board** (a Triple-A 2025 row gets Triple-A 2025 numbers, an MLB 2026 spring row gets spring numbers):

| Prefix | Source | What |
|---|---|---|
| `bats`, `throws`, `birth_date`, `age`, `height_in`, `weight_lb`, `primary_position`, `mlb_debut_date`, `birth_country` | MLB StatsAPI `/people` | Bio; `age` is on June 30 of the row's season |
| `api_bat_*` | MLB StatsAPI season hitting (batter and catcher rows) | PA, AB, H, HR, SO, BB, AVG, OBP, SLG, OPS, pitches seen |
| `api_pit_*` | MLB StatsAPI season pitching (pitcher rows) | BF, IP, SO, BB, HR, ERA, WHIP, strike share, pitches |
| `api_c_*` | MLB StatsAPI fielding at C (catcher rows) | Innings, stolen bases allowed, caught stealing, passed balls, catcher ERA |
| `sc_bat_*` / `sc_pit_*` | Statcast search aggregated by player (as batter / against pitcher) | Swings, takes, whiffs, chase % (zones 11-14), zone swing % and zone contact % (zones 1-9), share of pitches with a zone, xwOBA, xBA, xSLG, exit velocity, hard-hit %, barrels |
| `sc_c_*` | Statcast search as catcher (`fielder_2`) | Pitches received; called-strike % on taken pitches outside the zone and called-ball % on taken pitches inside it (as recorded by Statcast) |
| `api_bat_woba`, `api_bat_wrc_plus`, `api_bat_war`, `api_pit_war`, `api_pit_fip`, `api_pit_xfip`, `sc_c_framing_*` | StatsAPI sabermetrics, Savant catcher-framing leaderboard | **MLB 2026 regular season rows only** (framing: qualified catchers only) |

Official Savant leaderboards such as framing exist only for MLB regular seasons, so Triple-A and spring rows get the same kind of numbers from the Statcast search instead. In MLB 2025 spring training (the ABS test) only about two thirds of pitches have a Statcast zone (99%+ on every other board), so that board's chase, zone and catcher zone columns rest on those pitches; `*_zone_tracked_percent` gives the share per player.

## How it was built and checked

Built in GitHub Actions by `build.py` in [yasumorishima/kaggle-datasets](https://github.com/yasumorishima/kaggle-datasets). The build writes nothing unless every gate passes:

- savant-extras raises if Savant answers with a season or level other than the one asked for (Savant silently ignores parameters it does not recognise and answers with a default board);
- no two boards, of any challenger type, may share more than 20% of their rows on (`player_id`, `n_total_sample`, `n_challenges`, `n_overturns`) (real boards share at most 1%);
- every board lists players with 0 challenges (the minimum of 0 was applied), and only catcher boards carry `fielder_2`;
- no duplicated `player_id` within a board, and a minimum row count per board;
- the count identities above hold;
- the bridge table has at least 150 batters and 40 catchers;
- every player id on every board is found by StatsAPI `/people`;
- StatsAPI replies (season and sabermetrics) carry the season asked for and have no duplicated player; the hitting replies tell spring from regular season (the largest spring plate-appearance total is at most 150, a regular season's at least 400);
- on every board, the batter and pitcher Statcast searches contain at least 90% of StatsAPI's players, with plate appearances matching StatsAPI's for at least 95% of them (within 1 in spring training; on regular-season boards within 8 for batters and 30 for pitchers, a game's worth, because Savant can trail StatsAPI by a game while a season is being played); a reply for another season covers about 62% of the players and one for another level about 46%;
- the catcher Statcast searches contain at least 90% of StatsAPI's catchers, the median pitches received per inning caught is between 12 and 22, and no zone count is empty;
- zone counts are consistent (zone pitches never exceed pitches, called pitches never exceed takes), no zone reply is empty, and the catcher-framing replies for 2025 and 2026 differ.

## Ideas

- Does Triple-A 2025 `overturns_vs_exp` predict MLB 2026 `overturns_vs_exp` for the same batter or catcher?
- Catchers challenge most often: which catchers win more than expected, and at which level did they learn it?
- How much do spring-training challenge habits (2025 test, 2026) carry into the regular season?
- Join to Statcast pitch data by `player_id` to see what kind of pitches players challenge.
- Do hitters with a low `sc_bat_chase_percent` (good zone judgement) win more of their challenges?
- Are catchers whose takes outside the zone are often called strikes (`sc_c_oz_called_strike_percent`, a framing proxy that also exists for Triple-A) better or worse challengers?
- Does age, handedness or experience (`mlb_debut_date`) relate to challenge rate or success?
